Maya (prod-platform): Heads-up — before we flip the new automatic fallback rollout, can we add a simple changelog + a deterministic 'what-if' replay in the console? need an audit trail that shows which rule fired and why so SREs can validate behavior.
Ben (eng): +1. Do you mean replay recorded requests against a policy snapshot, or just simulate decisions?
Maya (prod-platform): Ideally both. Replay real request traces (sanitized) against the exact policy commit so we can reproduce a decision path. Simulation-only is ok as a light-weight option.
Liam (design): For the UI I imagine a compact panel: policy diff, sample request picker, and a step-by-step decision trace. Minimal — don't overwhelm with raw logs. :eyes:
Zoe (oncall): Safety note — we must ensure replay doesn't leak PII. Also need opt-out for customer requests and a retention TTL for traces. And a button to 'export trace with redactions' for postmortems.
Carlos (eng-ml): From runtime side we can export request features we use for routing (model id, latency bucket, error type, quota state) at decision time. That should be sufficient to reproduce decisions without full payloads.
Ben (eng): Implementation idea: every policy commit gets an immutable snapshot id. We store a lightweight decision log: timestamp, snapshot_id, decision_path (list of rule ids), and a hash of request. Replayer takes a stored sample (or live trace) and re-evaluates against snapshot config.
Maya (prod-platform): Exactly. Also want a short human-friendly changelog entry per commit: author, reason, diff summary. UX should surface who changed the escape-hatch thresholds.
Liam (design): UX question — should we show simulated latency/cost impact estimates when toggling degrade modes? e.g., "switch to degrade-mode: cpu-shed -> estimated +30ms, -12% token-cost". That helps product and SREs pick tradeoffs.
Zoe (oncall): Very helpful. Also add a 'safety preview' that runs through a sampling of live traffic and reports how many requests would have flipped to fallback in the last hour/day. No raw bodies.
Ben (eng): We need to standardize rule ids and stable semantics. If rules are re-ordered we should still map historical decisions to the right rule id. That implies immutable identifiers in the policy DSL.
Carlos (eng-ml): Agreed. Also for ML model variants: replayer should map model aliases -> exact hash/version used at snapshot time, otherwise results will differ.
Maya (prod-platform): Thoughts on permissions? who can run a replay or export traces? I think only SRE + security + the original committer for 72h post-change.
Zoe (oncall): That sounds reasonable. Add an audit event for every replay with who ran it and what sample was used.
Ben (eng): Quick API sketch: POST /policies/{snapshot_id}/replay { sample_id: <id>, mode: dry-run|full } -> returns decision_trace_id. Then GET /decision_traces/{id} returns stepwise decisions.
Liam (design): We'll make a compact trace view: timeline with rule hits, hover for rule details, and a short summary banner: "N of M requests would have degraded" + risk hints.
devops-bot: deploy 3032109876 by Ben to staging succeeded :white_check_mark:
Maya (prod-platform): Nice. Action items: Ben to prototype snapshot+replay API, Carlos to define what runtime features we log, Liam to mock trace UI, Zoe to write retention/permissions constraints. I'll collect designs in the rollout doc.
Ben (eng): I'll open a PR with a minimal API and example payloads. Will include an export redaction checklist.
Carlos (eng-ml): I'll post the list of fields we can safely log (model_hash, route_tags, latency_bucket, status_code, rule_ids).
Zoe (oncall): I'll draft the permission matrix and retention TTL suggestions.
Maya (prod-platform): Thanks all. Let's aim to have a staging demo before the next release cadence. :rocket:
